'''Phillip Colella''' is an American applied mathematician and a member of the Applied Numerical Algorithms Group at the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]. He has also worked at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]]. He is known for his fundamental contributions in the development of mathematical methods and numerical tools used to solve [[partial differential equation]]s, including [[High-resolution scheme|high-resolution]] and [[adaptive mesh refinement]] schemes. Colella is a member of the US [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="hoise">{{cite web|date=2004-04-23|url=http://www.hoise.com/primeur/04/articles/monthly/AE-PR-05-04-49.html|title=Berkeley Lab computational scientist Phil Colella elected to National Academy of Sciences|publisher=hoise.com|accessdate=2009-11-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705144159/http://www.hoise.com/primeur/04/articles/monthly/AE-PR-05-04-49.html|archivedate=2008-07-05}}</ref>

==Career==
Colella received his bachelor's degree in 1974, Master's degree in 1976, and Ph.D. in 1979 degree from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], all in applied mathematics.<ref name="scidac">{{cite web|url=http://www.scidac.gov/Conference2006/poster_bio/ColellaBio.html|title=Phil Colella Short Bio|publisher=scidac.gov|accessdate=2009-11-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905154543/http://www.scidac.gov/Conference2006/poster_bio/ColellaBio.html|archivedate=2008-09-05}}</ref> He received the Ph.D. degree under the supervision of [[Alexandre Chorin]]. He began his research career at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], University of California, California. His primary area of research involves the development of high-resolution schemes and adaptive mesh refinement methods for the solution of partial differential equations. He has also applied [[Numerical method|computational methods]] in a variety of scientific and engineering fields, including low-speed [[incompressible flow]]s, [[Shock wave|shock wave theory]], [[combustion]], [[magnetohydrodynamics]], and astrophysical flows.<ref name="SIAMACM">{{cite web|url=http://awards.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1558975&srt=all&aw=151&ao=SIAMACM|title=ACM Award Citation / Phillip Colella|publisher=[[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]]|accessdate=2009-11-01|archive-date=2012-04-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419234325/http://awards.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1558975&srt=all&aw=151&ao=SIAMACM|url-status=dead}}</ref> Colella has also been the leader of a project in [[NASA]]'s Computational Technologies for Earth and Space Sciences, called "Block-Structured Adaptive Mesh Refinement Methods for Multiphase Microgravity Flows and Star Formation".<ref name="hoise" />

==Awards and honors==
Colella is a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] since 2004 and Fellow of [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2009|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|accessdate=2009-11-01}}</ref> He is the recipient of many honors, including the [[Sidney Fernbach Award]] from the [[IEEE Computer Society]] in 1998, given each year to one person who has made "an outstanding contribution in the application of high performance computers using innovative approaches."<ref name="fernbach">{{cite web|date=1998-11-03|url=http://www.nersc.gov/news/newsroom/fernbach11-3-98.php|title=Phillip Colella Receives 1998 Sidney Fernbach Award|publisher=[[National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center]]|accessdate=2009-11-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090802070551/http://www.nersc.gov/news/newsroom/fernbach11-3-98.php|archivedate=2009-08-02}}</ref> He has also received the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]/[[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]] prize (with [[John B. Bell (mathematician)|John Bell]]) for computational science and engineering in 2003.<ref name="siam_acm">{{cite web|date=2003-09-30|url=http://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=343|title=LBNL Researchers Bell and Colella Receive First SIAM/ACM Prize in CSE|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|accessdate=2009-11-01}}</ref>
